S064-01.notes: Colon clause (support withdrawn, construction stopped, tower torn down) shows the plans never came to fruition: 'unrealized'. 'Secret' has no support (plans were public); 'profitable' is contradicted; 'conventional' is contradicted by wireless power. Facts (early 1900s, Long Island, Morgan, 1917 demolition) accurate.

S064-02.notes: Most manuscripts were moved out; militants still burned several thousand of those that remained, so without evacuation losses would likely have been far greater. A contradicts 'most' moved / 'several thousand' of hundreds of thousands burned. C reverses the logic. D unsupported (centuries of family use). Facts consistent with Haidara-led evacuation and the ~4,000 burned at the Ahmed Baba Institute in Jan 2013.

S064-03.notes: Preference = share of visits. 48/64 = 75%, 30/60 = 50%; both percentages correct. B (absolute drop in blue) is the main trap: a drop in total activity would not show weaker preference. C shows afternoon parity only, no comparison to morning. D is totals, irrelevant to preference.

S064-04.notes: Text 2: chinampas did not float; willow roots anchored them to lake bed. A contradicts 'did not float' and 'fertile'. B and D unsupported/contradicted (built in shallow water). Facts accurate.

S064-05.notes: Text describes the survey and then the uses (baseline, standards). C is a detail; A and D unsupported. Facts broadly accurate (1887 survey, ~40,000 samples, normal-chlorine map, early US standards). The sentence attributes elevated chlorine to sewage only in populated areas via the relative clause, which reads acceptably (coastal chlorine is natural sea-salt influence); not flagged.

S064-06.notes: Complete independent clause precedes a list that elaborates 'three stages' -> colon. B: semicolon not followed by independent clause. C: 'such as:' is incorrect (colon after 'such as' and the list is exhaustive, not examples). D: run-on fusion 'three stages his childhood'. Facts (1927-28 interviews, Cudjo Lewis, Clotilda, community near Mobile) accurate.

S064-07.notes: Subject is singular 'collection' (with intervening 'Bronzes' and a long nonrestrictive clause as the agreement trap); past passive 'was transferred' fits 'in 2022'. A plural; B plural and perfect clashes with specific past date; C nonfinite, leaves no main verb. Fact acceptable: German public museums' Benin Bronzes (~1,100+) transferred to Nigerian ownership in 2022; many looted in the 1897 British expedition.

S064-08.notes: Shift from 1937-1960 neglect to post-1975 revival: temporal 'Decades later'. D 'As a result' is the trap but the revival was not caused by being out of print/mixed reviews (it is a reversal). A and B wrong relationships. Facts (1937, out of print by 1960, Walker's 1975 Ms. essay) accurate.

flags.note: In B, 'its captives' has no clear antecedent: the Clotilda is never named in the sentence (the nearest nouns are 'Africatown residents' and, after, 'the 2019 discovery'), so the pronoun reads as Africatown's captives. Consider 'many descended from the ship's captives'. Also 'many' slightly overstates the notes, which say only that descendants still live there.

S064-09.notes: Only B connects the discovery to residents (descendants) and why it mattered (confirmed a history hidden by burning the ship). A states the discovery without significance to residents; C and D omit the discovery. Facts accurate (arrived 1860, burned, Africatown, wreck confirmed 2019).

S064-10.notes: Claim is comparative: direct experience of nature is more meaningful than scientific explanation. D shows the speaker leaving the lecture to look at the stars 'in perfect silence', i.e., embracing direct experience. C (tired and sick) is the strongest trap but shows only discontent with the lecture, not the positive value of nature. A and B describe the lecture neutrally. Quotations checked against the 1865 text and are accurate; D begins mid-line ('Till rising and gliding out I wander'd off by myself'), which is acceptable excerpting.
